    Transfer¶

    rn_forge.fastapi.transfer ¶

    Tabular export and import, and batch get, create, update and delete, over FastAPI.

    Requires the transfer extra. Not imported by :mod:rn_forge.fastapi. Persistence is the application's: the route factories take a store dependency that implements one of the store protocols, and :func:read_rows validates without saving.

    BatchCreateStore ¶

    Bases: Protocol

    Persists a batch of new resources.

    create_many(items) async ¶

    Create every item in one transaction and return the created objects.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    ItemsDenied

    An item is not permitted, raised before anything is written.

    BatchDeleteStore ¶

    Bases: Protocol

    Finds and deletes a batch of resources.

    delete_many(ids) async ¶

    Delete every id in one transaction.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    ItemsDenied

    An id may not be deleted, raised before anything is deleted.

    find(ids) async ¶

    Return which of ids exist within the caller's scope.

    BatchGetStore ¶

    Bases: Protocol

    Finds a batch of resources.

    get_many(ids) async ¶

    Return the rows of ids that exist within the caller's scope, keyed by id as a string.

    BatchUpdateStore ¶

    Bases: Protocol

    Finds and updates a batch of resources.

    current(ids) async ¶

    Return each of ids that exists within the caller's scope, keyed by id as a string.

    update_many(items) async ¶

    Write every validated document in one transaction and return the updated rows.

    Bumps each versioned row's version. The rows are returned in the order of items.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    ItemsDenied

    An item is not permitted, with root="requests", raised before anything is written.

    Current ¶

    Bases: Protocol

    version property ¶

    batch_create_router(collection, *, model, response_model, resource_name, store, max_rows=None, dependencies=()) ¶

    Build POST {collection}:batchCreate, taking {"requests": [...]}.

    Every item is validated into model and every failure is reported, as a 422 problem pointing at /requests/<i>/<field>, and the store is not called. The response is 200 with the created objects, as response_model dumped by alias, under resource_name.

    		 required

    		 required

    A dependency returning the :class:BatchCreateStore.

    		 required
    max_rows int | None

    The most items a batch may hold; None for no limit.

    		 None
    dependencies Sequence[Depends]

    Type Description

    The router.

    batch_delete_router(collection, *, resource_label, store, max_rows=None, dependencies=()) ¶

    Build POST {collection}:batchDelete, taking {"ids": [...]}.

    Ids may be strings or integers and are compared as strings. The first id that :meth:BatchDeleteStore.find does not return is a 404 reading {resource_label} {id} not found. The response is 204.

    A dependency returning the :class:BatchDeleteStore.

    		 required

    The most ids a batch may hold; None for no limit.

    		 None
    dependencies Sequence[Depends]

    The router.

    batch_get_router(collection, *, response_model, resource_name, resource_label, store, max_rows=None, read_mask=True, dependencies=()) ¶

    Build GET {collection}:batchGet, taking a repeated ids query parameter.

    A missing ids parameter, or more ids than max_rows, is a 400 problem. The first id that :meth:BatchGetStore.get_many does not return is a 404 reading {resource_label} {id} not found. The response is 200 with one entry per requested id, in request order and repeating duplicates, as response_model dumped by alias, under resource_name. With read_mask, the route also takes readMask (see :func:rn_forge.fastapi.read_mask_param) and each resource holds only the fields it names.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    collection str

    The collection path, for example /orders.

    		 required
    response_model type[BaseModel]

    The model of one resource.

    		 required
    resource_name str

    The response member that holds the resources.

    		 required
    resource_label str

    The resource's name in the 404 detail, for example Order.

    		 required
    store Callable[..., BatchGetStore]

    A dependency returning the :class:BatchGetStore.

    		 required
    max_rows int | None

    The most ids a batch may hold; None for no limit.

    		 None
    read_mask bool

    Whether the route accepts readMask.

    		 True
    dependencies Sequence[Depends]

    Dependencies of the route, as for APIRouter.

    		 ()

    Returns:

    Type Description
    APIRouter

    The router.

    batch_update_router(collection, *, model, response_model, resource_name, resource_label, store, max_rows=None, require_if_match=False, codec=None, dependencies=()) ¶

    Build POST {collection}:batchUpdate, taking {"requests": [...]}.

    Each item is {"id", "patch", "ifMatch"}: patch is a JSON Merge Patch and ifMatch an optional precondition. The current row is dumped through model by alias, merged with the patch and validated as model. The first failing step answers: the list and item shape are 422 problems, a missing id is a 404 reading {resource_label} {id} not found, a failed precondition is a 428, 400 or 412 pointing at /requests/<i>/ifMatch, and an invalid merged document is a 422 problem pointing at /requests/<i>/patch/<field>. The store is not asked to write after a failure. Ids may be strings or integers and are compared as strings. The response is 200 with the updated rows, as response_model dumped by alias, under resource_name.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    collection str

    The collection path, for example /orders.

    		 required
    model type[T]

    The model of one full resource document.

    		 required
    response_model type[BaseModel]

    The model of one updated resource.

    		 required
    resource_name str

    The response member that holds the updated resources.

    		 required
    resource_label str

    The resource's name in the 404 detail, for example Order.

    		 required
    store Callable[..., BatchUpdateStore[T]]

    A dependency returning the :class:BatchUpdateStore.

    		 required
    max_rows int | None

    The most items a batch may hold; None for no limit.

    		 None
    require_if_match bool

    When True, a versioned item without ifMatch is a 428.

    		 False
    codec ETagCodec | None

    The validator format; None uses :class:rn_forge.web.VersionETagCodec.

    		 None
    dependencies Sequence[Depends]

    Dependencies of the route, as for APIRouter.

    		 ()

    Type Description

    The router.

    import_router(collection, *, model, store, formats=('csv', 'xlsx'), max_rows=None, dependencies=()) ¶

    Build POST {collection}:import, a multipart upload of a file part.

    Each row is validated into model, whose aliases are the column headers. Any failed row answers a 422 problem and nothing reaches the store. The validateOnly query parameter is parsed by :func:~rn_forge.web.transfer.parse_flag. The response is 200 with :func:~rn_forge.web.transfer.import_report_body.

    import_template_router(collection, *, model, source, formats=('csv', 'xlsx'), max_rows=None, dependencies=()) ¶

    Build GET {collection}:importTemplate, the import columns as a file.

    The format is negotiated as for :func:tabular_format, else the first of formats. The columns are model's aliases, so the file round-trips through :func:import_router. Without prefill the file holds the header row only; with it, the rows of :class:TemplateSource. The download is named import-template.<ext>.

    problem_response(problem) ¶

    Send a rendered problem, such as row_errors_problem(...), as a response.

    read_rows(upload, model, *, formats=_READABLE) async ¶

    Load upload with tablib and validate each row against model.

    The format comes from the file extension, else from the part's content type, among formats. Row indexes are zero-based positions after the header row. An error's field is the column header (the model's alias); a validator that raises ValueError reports its own message. total is the number of data rows read.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    upload UploadFile

    The uploaded file.

    		 required
    model type[T]

    The row model.

    		 required
    formats Sequence[str]

    The accepted extensions, a subset of csv, tsv and xlsx.

    		 _READABLE

    Raises:

    Type Description
    ValueError

    The file's type is not in formats, with :func:~rn_forge.web.transfer.unsupported_file_detail as its message, or its content cannot be parsed, with :func:~rn_forge.web.transfer.unreadable_file_detail.

    tabular_format(allowed=('csv', 'xlsx')) ¶

    Return a dependency yielding the tabular format the request asks for.

    The format query parameter wins over Accept; see :func:rn_forge.web.transfer.negotiate_tabular_format. The dependency yields None when the response should be the endpoint's JSON.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    allowed Iterable[str]

    The extensions the endpoint offers.

    		 ('csv', 'xlsx')

    tabular_response(rows, model, fmt, filename) async ¶

    Render rows as a file download in fmt.

    Each row is validated into model with from_attributes=True and dumped by alias, so the model's serialization aliases are the column headers and its computed fields are columns. Use serialization_alias for a header that differs from the attribute name: a plain alias would also rename the attribute read from an ORM object. CSV is streamed; the other formats are built in memory in a worker thread.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    rows Iterable[Any]

    ORM objects, mappings or model instances.

    		 required
    model type[BaseModel]

    The export model.

    		 required
    fmt TabularFormat

    The chosen format.

    		 required
    filename str

    The download name, extension included.

    		 required

    Returns:

    Type Description
    Response

    A StreamingResponse for CSV, otherwise a Response.
